sample_size.excerpt: In this secondary analysis of the Women’s Health Initiative Observational Study that included 80 388 postmenopausal women, higher consumption of artificially sweetened beverages was associated with a higher risk of kidney cancer.

studies.Title: Artificial sweetener use and bladder cancer: a case-control study.
studies.Reference: Artificial sweetener use and bladder cancer: a case-control study.
studies.Population: Bladder cancer patients and matched hospital patient controls

extraction_supporting_text.cases: In a case-control study of 302 male and 65 female bladder cancer patients and an equal number of other patients matched to them in age, sex, hospital, and hospital-room status, no association was found between use of artificial sweeteners or diet beverages and bladder cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.design: In a case-control study of 302 male and 65 female bladder cancer patients and an equal number of other patients matched to them in age, sex, hospital, and hospital-room status, no association was found between use of artificial sweeteners or diet beverages and bladder cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.exposure_measurement: No dose-response was observed with respect to quantity or duration of use of the two combined.
extraction_supporting_text.gender: In a case-control study of 302 male and 65 female bladder cancer patients and an equal number of other patients matched to them in age, sex, hospital, and hospital-room status, no association was found between use of artificial sweeteners or diet beverages and bladder cancer.
extraction_supporting_text.smoking_status: No evidence was found to suggest that artificial sweeteners or diet beverages promote the tumorigenic effect of tobacco smoking.

extraction_supporting_text.sample_size: Using data on 1,860 bladder cancer cases and 3,934 population-based controls from the National Bladder Cancer Study, we examined associations between suspected bladder cancer risk factors and tumor stage and grade.
extraction_supporting_text.cases: Using data on 1,860 bladder cancer cases and 3,934 population-based controls from the National Bladder Cancer Study, we examined associations between suspected bladder cancer risk factors and tumor stage and grade.
extraction_supporting_text.comparison: Heavy artificial sweetener use was associated with higher-grade, poorly differentiated tumors.
